question: In △ABC, BD ⟂ AC at D and ∠DBC = 76°. E is a point on BC such that ∠CAE = 74°. What is the measure of ∠AEB?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In right-angled △BDC, ∠C = 90° − ∠DBC = 90° − 76° = 14°.

In △AEC, the exterior angle at vertex E is equal to the sum of its two interior opposite angles.

⇒ ∠AEB = ∠CAE + ∠C

⇒ ∠AEB = 74° + 14° = 88°.

**∴ The correct answer is 88°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

BD ⊥ AC at point D, implying ∠BDC = 90°

∠DBC = 76°

∠CAE = 74°

**Calculations:**

Consider the right-angled triangle BDC formed by altitude BD:

⇒ ∠C + ∠DBC + ∠BDC = 180°

⇒ ∠C + 76° + 90° = 180°

⇒ ∠C = 180° − 166°

⇒ ∠C = 14°

Now, observe the triangle AEC. The point E lies on the segment BC. Hence, the angle ∠AEB forms an exterior angle to △AEC at vertex E.

According to the Exterior Angle Theorem, an exterior angle is strictly equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles of the triangle:

⇒ ∠AEB = ∠CAE + ∠ACE

⇒ ∠AEB = 74° + ∠C

⇒ ∠AEB = 74° + 14°

⇒ ∠AEB = 88°

**∴ The correct answer is 88°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the measures of its two remote interior angles. Formula: ∠Exterior = ∠Opposite₁ + ∠Opposite₂

Triangle Angle Sum Property

The total measure of the internal angles of any valid triangle is strictly 180°. In right-angled triangles, the two non-right (acute) angles must complement each other (sum to exactly 90°).

Linear Pair Axiom

When two adjacent angles form a straight continuous line, they are called a linear pair and are supplementary. Therefore, their sum is always equal to 180°.
